system_overview: This specification refines the basic PCR (Polymerase Chain Reaction) model by adding a stage-tracking history variable and a cycle counter. In the basic model, temperature transitions could occur in any order; this refinement constrains them to follow the correct thermocycling sequence: denaturation, cooling, annealing, extension. The stage variable records the most recent completed phase, ensuring that each phase can only execute when the preceding phase has been completed. This enables counting the number of complete PCR cycles and proving that primers are eventually depleted.
actors_and_components: The system has no concurrent actors. It models a single PCR reaction vessel. The molecular components are the same as in the basic model: double-stranded DNA, single-stranded templates, primers, and primer-template hybrids.
state_variables: The system tracks seven quantities: (1) the current temperature phase (three levels as in the basic model); (2) the count of available primers; (3) the count of double-stranded DNA molecules; (4) the count of single-stranded templates; (5) the count of primer-template hybrids; (6) a stage indicator recording which phase was most recently completed, taking values from: initial, denatured, ready (cooled), annealed, or extended; (7) a cycle counter tracking how many complete PCR cycles have been executed.
initial_state: Temperature is at extension level. Primer and DNA counts equal their respective initial constants. Templates and hybrids are zero. The stage is set to the initial value. The cycle counter is zero.
actions: Four actions model the constrained PCR cycle: (1) Heating: enabled only when the stage is initial or extended. Raises temperature, denatures all DNA and hybrids into templates, recovers primers from hybrids. Sets stage to denatured. (2) Cooling: enabled only when the stage is denatured. Lowers temperature. No molecular changes. Sets stage to ready. (3) Annealing: enabled only when the stage is ready. A nondeterministic number of primers bind to templates, forming hybrids. Sets stage to annealed. (4) Extension: enabled only when the stage is annealed. All hybrids become double-stranded DNA. Increments the cycle counter. Sets stage to extended. The molecular transformations in each action are identical to the basic model.
safety_properties: Type correctness: temperature, molecular counts, stage indicator, and cycle counter are all within their expected domains.
liveness_properties: Primer depletion: eventually all primers are consumed. This property holds in this refinement (unlike the basic model) because weak fairness on all four actions ensures continuous cycling, and each cycle consumes at least one primer.
model_bounds: Initial DNA and primer counts are declared as constants. For model checking, typical values are 5 for each. Deadlock checking is disabled because the system reaches a terminal state when primers are exhausted.
additional_assumptions: Weak fairness is assumed on all four temperature-cycling actions, ensuring that the system continuously progresses through PCR cycles and does not stutter indefinitely. This module refines the basic PCR specification: every behavior of this specification is also a behavior of the basic model. The stage variable acts as a history variable constraining the order of operations without changing the molecular dynamics.
